architecture_fit_summary: Proposed VPC topology: separate management and runtime subnets across AZs; runtime in private subnets with no public IPs; management subnet for admins and bastion hosts

Networking: prefer Transit Gateway architecture to allow central egress control; alternative is VPC peering + shared services VPC. Customer network team leaning toward Transit Gateway for multi-region scale

Outbound/inbound rules: inbound only from customer NAT/bastion for admin SSH (restricted), inference traffic initiated from customer clients to internal ALB (TLS); outbound restricted to Redwood control-plane PrivateLink endpoints + S3 endpoints for logs/weights
Private connectivity: implement AWS PrivateLink for Redwood control-plane (control-plane calls over VPC endpoint), S3 VPC endpoints for model artifact storage, Secrets Manager KMS VPC endpoints

KMS integration: customer-managed CMK in their account with HSM-backed key; Redwood service principal granted decrypt/encrypt via cross-account key policy; keys must never be exported. Key rotation policy required and annual attestation

Audit logging: CloudTrail enabled in all regions, logs delivered to S3 bucket in customer account (restricted), logs forwarded to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector. Provide mapping doc for token-level events to CloudTrail entries

Data residency: models and transient KV caches for EU data pinned to eu-west-1; control plane can be global but control-plane metadata stored encrypted and region-tagged. No model/embedding outputs copied across regions without explicit consent
Egress policy: only outbound to allowlisted IPs/FQDNs; all other internet traffic blocked. Use NAT or Egress-only gateway for controlled updates to container images/artifacts
Admin access: multi-hop bastion + SSO/SAML enforced; session audit logs stored to central SIEM
Secrets & rotation: recommend Secrets Manager + CMK; provide sample IAM role policies and least-privilege model for inference nodes
